text:
maria: FYI rolling cu12 image to eu-west triggered a flurry of container restarts on long-lived pods, hitting linker errors and signal 6 crashes. noticed during the overnight canary.
alex: any logs yet? node or container level?
maria: container logs from one pod pasted below — looks like an unresolved C++ symbol during dlopen:
```
python3: /opt/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12: undefined symbol: __gxx_personality_v0
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
Aborted (core dumped)
```
sam: that screams compiler/runtime mismatch. libc++/libstdc++ ABI mismatch between the image toolchain and the host's loader/runtime. did we rebuild base images with gcc13 for cu12?
julien: yes — the new cu12 images were built on builder nodes using distro packages (gcc-13). older host kernels / glibc combinations on some fleets still expect the older libstdc++. We saw this in a couple of non-prod clusters but didn't expect it at this scale.
devops-bot: detected 18 pods with crashloopbackoff across eu-west-gpu-pool-2, auto-drain requested on 3 nodes (reason: incompatible-runtime). logs archived to s3://redwood-ops/logs/cu12-failures/2025-03-08
maria: pinned a couple of critical services to the previous `redwood/cuda:11.8-prod-202502` image — that stabilizes them, but a lot of model-serving jobs are still impacted.
alex: can we avoid rebuilds by shipping a compatibility shim? maybe bundle `libstdc++.so.6` from the older toolchain into the app image and set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
sam: we tried that for one microservice — it worked but caused a subtle symbol collision for plugins. it's a risky band-aid at scale.
julien: tradeoffs: (1) rebuild all images with gcc-11 toolchain (takes ~6-8h of CI + image push + node rolling), (2) change host stacks to accept newer ABI (kernel/glibc constraints, longer), (3) per-image shims and testing (less infra churn but fragile).
maria: product impact: two Dedicated customers reported degraded throughput; one started failing health checks. ops-sre is monitoring.
oncall-bot: incident created: INFRA-4123 (cu12 image / libstdc++ ABI regressions). Priority: P1 for eu-west model fleet. Pager notification sent to oncall.
alex: immediate mitigation plan: (A) pin critical prod services to cuda11 images (done for a subset), (B) hold further cu12 image deploys in eu-west and asia until canary passes in a small opt-in pool, (C) schedule bulk image rebuilds with gcc-11 in CI and publish compatibility tag `cuda12-compat-gcc11`.
sam: cost note — rebuilding ~1.2k images will consume significant CI/mirror bandwidth and outbound egress; estimate ~12k build-minutes and spike in our ECR pushes. finance FYI for short-term quota bump?
julien: also need a longer-term policy: every toolkit bump must include a host compatibility matrix (kernel/glibc/gcc) and an automated canary runway that exercises long-lived pods, not just fast start/stop tests.
maria: agreed. creating a follow-up doc for rollout gating and compatibility checklist. @alex can you own the rebuild job? @julien can you own the canary policy?
alex: yes, I'll start the `cuda12-compat-gcc11` pipeline and prioritize the top 200 images used by model-serving.
julien: I'll draft the canary policy and add a preflight that runs a 24h long-lived pod test with `LD_PRELOAD` variants.
maria: thanks — keep updates in this thread. I'll coordinate with customer success for the Dedicated customer notifications. :pray:
alex: quick note — we should advertise this to infra partners: avoid surprise host upgrades and ensure toolkit + distro toolchain pinning.
sam: tl;dr: downgrade images or rebuild with older compiler for now; gate future toolkit bumps behind a canary suite that stresses long-lived processes.
maria: logging final: rolling back further cu12 pushes in eu-west, canary paused, incident INFRA-4123 open. continuing in #incidents for postmortem.
